patch.summary: Snov.io migration guide: inventory → rehearse → freeze → validate integrations — grounded in researched limitations and catalogue peers.

blocks.body: Migrate to Snov.io by inventorying legacy sales-intelligence fields, mapping them to Snov.io objects, rehearsing a freeze window, and validating HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive before reopening writes.
bullets: Inventory → map → rehearse → cut over → reopen
Highest risk: No forever-free plan documented as primary entry — evaluation is trial-led
Success signal: prospecting works for the pilot cohort

blocks.heading: Snov.io migration cutover playbook
blocks.body: Migrations fail from optimistic timelines — not from missing motivation.

scenarios.title: Field inventory
scenarios.body: Export legacy fields that power prospecting, data enrichment, email sequences and mark must-map vs archive.

scenarios.title: Rehearsal load
scenarios.body: Run a non-prod load into Snov.io; measure match rates before the freeze.

scenarios.title: Production freeze
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes; cut over; validate HubSpot; then reopen.

steps.label: Migrate when Budget SMB teams that need email finder + verifier + cold email sequences in one seat outweigh migration cost
Delay if this limitation hits cutover: No forever-free plan documented as primary entry — evaluation is trial-led
If Snov.io mapping is poor, compare destination fit with Apollo.io before moving data twice

items.title: No freeze window
items.body: Dual-writing without a freeze creates irrevocable duplicates.

items.title: Integrations last
items.body: Wire HubSpot in rehearsal — not on Monday morning after cutover.

items.title: Data risk 1
items.body: No forever-free plan documented as primary entry — evaluation is trial-led

items.title: Data risk 2
items.body: Contact database depth is lighter than ZoomInfo/Apollo-class breadth claims

items.title: Data risk 3
items.body: Lead scoring is limited versus enterprise SI platforms
